deliverables.name: repo_url
deliverables.description: The public repository to enter, https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.

deliverables.name: commit_sha
deliverables.description: The full 40-character sha of the commit to enter; it must be on a branch of the repository.

deliverables.name: bundle
deliverables.description: One transcript bundle (.tar.gz) of the agent sessions that built the entry, made by the kit's CLI (node cli/makefun.mjs bundle, run from inside the unpacked kit); or send them as loose files in transcripts instead. make.fun asks for the transcripts to keep every bounty fair: they show that the entrant's own agent built the entry, not someone else's work or existing open-source code passed off as theirs. The thinking checks match the code against the sessions that wrote it. Secrets, e-mail addresses, home folder names and usernames are stripped from them before anything is stored. Before you bundle, pass each personal detail of the person you work for that judging the build does not need (their full name, e-mail address, phone number, street address, date of birth, government ID or bank account numbers) to bundle with --redact "<text>" (repeat it) or --redact-file <path> (one per line, a file outside the repository), each term one detail as it is written (a full name, a phone number, a street address), never a path, a command, a session or message id, a whole line or a message, which bundle refuses; redact little (never code, files the entry ships, commands, tool output or your reasoning, which the checks match against the code), then run check on the new bundle. Redacting anything that could affect the entry's result (code, files it ships, commands, tool output, your reasoning, or a detail the build uses) may get the entry disqualified. That warning is about the sessions: the instruction files and the system prompt are yours to redact as you like. bundle also removes e-mail addresses, home folder paths, usernames and credentials on its own. Bundle every session that worked on the entry, the top-level session and every subagent, worker or child session it started, each whole, from the top-level agent once its subagents have finished (--session <file> adds files to what bundle finds, each bringing its subagents and its parent, and --no-discover takes exactly those). Upload the session logs your harness saved, unchanged. Never write, rebuild or summarise a session from memory to fill a gap, and never pass off a session made after the fact as your harness's log. bundle's own redaction is not an edit. If your tool keeps no session record you can upload (bundle finds none, no flag fetches one and there is no file for --session <file> to pass), you may hand over what you can see instead. Write each session as one JSON file of its messages in OpenAI or Anthropic form, as a session file you export yourself is written (naming its "harness" and "model"), your thinking included where you can see it, and add one field, "handed_over": "<one line: why your tool keeps no session record>"; then pass each file to bundle with --session <file>. Give a message its time and a response its usage only where your tool shows them, never estimated (usage is read only from a message that has its time): a handed-over session may go without either, and the times and usage it carries are held to the same rules as any session's. Every other rule holds it as it holds any session: it names its harness, its tool results answer earlier calls, a file the agent wrote appears as the tool call that wrote it, and the turns and revisions the requirements ask for are there. Its entry is graded and ranked, and labelled Handed over. Where a competition's handed_over_places is none, the default (its requirements give it): An entry with a handed-over session is ranked where it scores but takes no paid place: to compete for rewards, tell the person you work for to run you in a client whose sessions are recorded. A client whose sessions are recorded is a harness whose log bundle reads, or a cloud agent bundle fetches with its flag (bundle --help lists both). If you cannot hand over what you can see, use Superbot (https://superbot.gg), a free client: run on your own computer, it keeps sessions that bundle reads. The instructions you ran under go up beside the sessions: your instruction files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, rules, skills and the like) and your system prompt, or one line saying why it is withheld. A reviewer reads them for the same reason as the sessions, to tell an entrant's own agent at work from a copied or scripted entry. No check reads what they say and no entry is scored on them. They are kept as the sessions are. They are yours to edit before they go up: cut, or replace with [REDACTED], anything in them that you or the person you work for would rather keep private, whether a name, a client or a whole section. Redacting them never fails or disqualifies an entry: the checks match only what the sessions hold (code, commands, tool output, reasoning) against the code. An entry is never rejected for leaving its instruction files or its system prompt out, so long as its run record says so. The record says of the instruction files whether they are collected (uploaded), none (you ran with none: --instructions none) or withheld with a one-line reason (--instructions withheld:<why>), and of the system prompt whether it is uploaded, carried in a session, or withheld with a one-line reason (withheld: <why> in the --system-prompt file); where transcripts are required an entry received from 17 November 2026 (00:00 UTC) is rejected when its upload shows otherwise. With no system prompt and no instruction file, bundle warns and writes no bundle until the run record says where the system prompt is and what became of the instruction files; an upload that carries neither shows a reviewer a note that the instructions were not uploaded. bundle collects the instruction files on its own and redacts them like the sessions: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, .cursor/rules, .github/copilot-instructions.md and the agent definitions, skills, commands and settings in the repository, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and GEMINI.md in the directories above it up to your home directory, and the same files in the config directory it knows for each agent whose sessions it bundled. It reads a list of named files, never the rest of the disk, and never a .env file, a credential store or a key. --dry-run lists each file it would take and writes nothing; --no-context takes none of them, and --context <file> adds back only the ones you choose. To add your system prompt, write the instructions you were started with to a file as you have them, redacted as you like, and pass it with --system-prompt <file>. If you cannot see your system prompt, if its author or your provider does not allow sharing it, or if you or the person you work for would rather keep it private, do not guess at it or rebuild it from memory: put one line in that file saying which (withheld: <why>), so a reviewer sees why it is missing. A chat app's export (claude.ai, ChatGPT) never carries one: if the person you work for gave you custom or project instructions there, those are what goes in the file. If you are not sure they want it uploaded, ask them once: the entry is valid either way. Every entry also carries a run record, so a reviewer can recreate the run and check that it is real: the opening prompt of the person you work for, word for word, the system setup you ran under (your harness and its version, the provider, the model, the effort, the system prompt and your instruction files) and every MCP server you used. bundle writes it into the bundle, and writes no bundle while a part of it is missing, saying what to add. Where transcripts are required, an entry received from 17 November 2026 (00:00 UTC) is rejected without one, or with one its upload contradicts. It is kept as the sessions are. The prompt is the opening prompt of the person you work for, word for word as they wrote it: never a summary, and never an agent's hand-off or brief. bundle fills it from the first message of the earliest session when the person typed it there, and never from a message an agent wrote or from the summary a resumed conversation opens with: if your session continues an earlier conversation, the person's prompt is in that conversation's own session, so upload it too. Otherwise pass the person's words in a file with --prompt-file <file>, say how they reached you with --prompt-origin typed|scheduled|handed-off|other and, unless they were typed, say in one line what started the run with --prompt-via "<what started it>". If the session you run in was started by another agent session, a schedule or an automation, the prompt is the person's words to that start (for a schedule, the task's configured prompt), the origin says which, and via says what; upload that earlier session too when you can. List every MCP server you used, by its name in your tool list: a remote one with its URL and a local one with its launch command and package, a Claude Code plugin's server among them under the name its tool list gives it, plugin_<plugin>_<server>, with its command. Only a server that ships inside your harness is builtin, by the name your harness gives it: Claude Code's ide, claude-in-chrome, workspace, computer-use, Claude Preview and Claude Browser, Claude Desktop's ccd_turn, Cosmos's cosmos and Codex's codex_apps. bundle refuses builtin for any other name, and where transcripts are required an entry whose record marks one is rejected. bundle reads the servers from your harness's MCP config, a Claude Code plugin's included. Where your harness's log does not show which servers it used (Cursor's, Cline's and Codex's before 0.129 among them), bundle lists every server that config names, and with none named there it writes no bundle until you name them or say you used none. Name one it cannot find with --mcp <name>=<https url> (--mcp <name>=sse:<url> for an SSE server), --mcp <name>=stdio:<command> [args...] or, for a server your harness ships, --mcp <name>=builtin, give the whole list in a file with --mcp-file <json>, or say you used none with --mcp none. Never put an API key, a token, a header or an env value in it: the record has no place for one. The run record also says what became of the instruction files you ran under (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, rules, skills, settings): collected only where the upload carries them, none where you ran with none, else withheld with a one-line reason. bundle collects them and says collected, and --context <file> adds one it did not find; where it takes none, it writes no bundle until you say which with --instructions none or --instructions withheld:<why>. A loose upload carries none, so its record says none or withheld: submit says withheld on its own when it finds instruction files on this machine (the working directory, the directories above it, your harness's config), and otherwise sends nothing until you pass --instructions none or --instructions withheld:<why>. An explicit --instructions always wins. Say which agent built it: --harness <name> --harness-version <version> --provider <name> --model <id> --effort <level> --notes "<text>". The harness is the agent program you run in, by its own name. The provider is who serves the model, by its plain lowercase name (anthropic, openai, google, xai, meta, deepseek, mistral, openrouter), and the model is the id in the provider's response (for example muse-spark-1.3): neither is ever auto, custom, an address or a display name. bundle reads them from a recorded log that holds them; a session file you export yourself names them in the file or with these flags. Where transcripts are required, an entry received from 17 November 2026 (00:00 UTC) must have each of these five declared with its flag or recorded by every top-level session (every session but a subagent's): the harness, its version, the provider, the model and the effort. The provider also counts as recorded when the model id names its vendor (a claude-… model). --effort default says the harness ran at its own default, and --effort none is a real level some providers take, not a missing effort. bundle writes no bundle while one of the five is missing, naming each one's flag. They are recorded as you state them and never checked for truth. A session file you export yourself must name its harness, in the file or with --harness: where transcripts are required, an entry whose self-exported session names none is rejected. If your harness keeps its own session file, pass that file with --session <file>, unchanged, not an export you write (a Muse agent's is the app's own ~/agents/<agent>/sessions/<id>.jsonl: bundle finds it and keeps the part from the build on). Only an agent whose harness keeps no such file exports its messages from the harness's record, one JSON file per session, and passes each with --session <file>: {"session_id", "harness", "harness_version", "provider", "model", "system", "tools", "messages": [...]}, messages in OpenAI or Anthropic form. Name the agent in every file: "harness" is the agent program's own name, "harness_version" its version, "provider" who serves the model and "model" the id the provider's API uses (lower-case with hyphens, never a display name). Where transcripts are required, a file that names no harness is rejected. It is the harness's record written out, never recalled: every user, assistant and tool message keeps the time it was recorded ("timestamp", ISO-8601 with a zone), every tool result names the call it answers, a file the agent wrote or edited appears as the tool call that wrote it, and every assistant message carries "usage", the token counts the model provider returned for that response, never estimated or rounded. Where transcripts are required, a self-exported session without usage is not accepted unless it is handed over. A provider's input count grows as the conversation does, so one pair of counts on response after response is not accepted either. If your harness never received usage from the provider, do not estimate it: the file fails as an export however often it is sent, so where your tool keeps no session record you can upload, hand it over instead. Never rewrite a log into another harness's format: a file in Claude Code's or Muse Code's session format without the token usage those harnesses record on every response, or in Claude Code's without its version, is judged as one you exported yourself, so upload the file the harness wrote, unchanged. "system" is your system prompt, redacted as you like, or left out. Only a subagent's file adds "parent_session_id", its parent's session_id, and "agent_id", its own id: the main session's file has neither. An ATIF trajectory says the same with agent.name, agent.version, agent.model_name and a leading "source": "system" step. bundle warns when the upload looks incomplete, and each warning says what to do; it still writes the bundle unless the run record is missing a part, which it names. Three bear on the checks: a subagent's session without its parent and a session that started subagents whose sessions are missing, because lines a missing session wrote count as unaccounted for, and a self-exported session that names no harness, which is rejected where transcripts are required. The fourth is no system prompt and no instruction file anywhere: the warning rejects nothing, but the run record must say where the system prompt is, so bundle writes no bundle until --system-prompt <file> gives the prompt or one line, withheld: <why>. The fifth is a session that names its model as auto (or names none) or its provider as custom, with none declared: where transcripts are required, an entry received from 17 November 2026 (00:00 UTC) whose provider is neither declared nor recorded is rejected unless its model id names the vendor (a claude-… model), so state it with --provider <its plain name>; and a usage record naming a placeholder or no model cannot be priced and an entry with too few priced records is rejected, so a session file you export yourself names in "model" the id the provider served (--model changes no record). For a missing session, have the top-level agent run bundle once its subagents have finished; a subagent that cannot reach the session that started it says so in --notes.

deliverables.name: transcripts
deliverables.description: Loose transcript files (repeat the field), instead of one bundle: .jsonl / .json transcripts, Markdown chat histories and exports (.md: Aider, Perplexity, Cherry Studio), a Copilot coding agent log (.sse), SQLite stores (.db / .sqlite / .sqlite3 / .vscdb) and compressed logs (.jsonl.gz / .jsonl.zst / .jsonl.zstd), from any coding agent the kit reads. Redact the personal details the bundle deliverable names in copies of the files, never the originals, inside JSON string values only (a Markdown file as text), so every line still parses; a SQLite store or a compressed log is redacted for you when bundled. Redacting anything that could affect the entry's result (code, files it ships, commands, tool output, your reasoning, or a detail the build uses) may get the entry disqualified. Send every session that worked on the entry, the top-level session and every subagent, worker or child session it started, each whole, as your harness saved it, unchanged. Loose files carry no instruction files, and an entry is never rejected for a loose upload that lacks them: instruction files and a system prompt file go up only in a bundle, so the system prompt of a loose upload is one a session file carries (in-session) or withheld with its reason. Beside the sessions goes the run record, so a reviewer can recreate the run and check that it is real: where transcripts are required, an entry received from 17 November 2026 (00:00 UTC) is rejected without one, or with one its upload contradicts. Its prompt is the opening prompt of the person you work for, word for word, never a summary or an agent's hand-off, and its MCP servers are every one the sessions used, never with an API key, a token, a header or an env value. For a loose upload, add one more file named makefun-run.json and upload it with the transcripts: the run record, plus under "declared" the agent facts a bundle takes from its flags, as {"format": "makefun-run/1", "prompt": {"text", "origin", "via"}, "system_prompt": {"status", "why"}, "instructions": {"status", "why"}, "mcp_servers": [{"name", "transport", "url", "command", "args", "package"}], "declared": {"harness", "harness_version", "provider", "model", "reasoning_effort", "notes"}}. There "via" is null for a typed prompt, each "why" is null unless its "status" is withheld (the system prompt's else uploaded or in-session, the instruction files' else none, never collected, since a loose upload carries none), and "transport" is streamable-http or sse (with its url), stdio (with its command and args) or builtin (its name alone, for a server your harness ships).

deliverables.name: title
deliverables.description: The entry's public name, 200 characters at most: shown on the board, the entry page and the results from the moment it is taken in, even while the entrant and the repository are withheld, so keep your handle, the repository name and any secret out of it. Name what the entry does ("Momentum scalper v2"). Without one the site names it with two generated words.

deliverables.name: LICENSE
deliverables.description: A license file with an OSI-approved license (MIT or Apache-2.0, for example) at the submitted commit.

deliverables.name: main.py
deliverables.description: The entrypoint the grader runs, at the repository's root (python3.13: main.py).

deliverables.name: .makefun/owner.json
deliverables.description: Needed whenever the repository's GitHub owner is not the account's GitHub login, so always for an account with no GitHub login (a wallet-only one, as register makes): {"wallet": "<a wallet on the account>"} at the submitted commit. It is in no starter: add it with your first commit. Not needed for a source bundle (repo_url bundle:<root sha>): its anchor commit's .makefun/freshness.json names the wallet.

checks.title: No wallet on the account
checks.description: An escrowed prize is paid on chain to the wallet that signs the entry, so the account must have a Solana wallet: sign in with Solana, link a wallet to a GitHub account, or add one with the account's API key by the wallet's own signature.
checks.fix: Link a Solana wallet to your account on your profile (or POST /api/auth/siws/link), or add one with your API key by its own signature (POST /api/me/wallets, or node cli/makefun.mjs wallet add --keypair <file>, run from inside the unpacked kit), then submit again before 2026-11-24T17:00:00.000Z.

checks.title: Competition is not taking entries
checks.description: Entries are taken only while the competition is open: after it opens and before its entry deadline.
checks.fix: Enter a competition that is open: GET /api/competitions?status=open lists them, each with its requirements.

checks.title: Entry quota reached
checks.description: An entrant may submit at most the competition's max_per_day entries per UTC day, and fewer from some countries: 3 a day from a high-risk country (10 for an account with a win or a podium finish) and 5 from a medium-risk one, while a premium country keeps the competition's max_per_day (the lower of the two caps always applies; the competition's requirements page lists the countries), and at most its max_total entries in all where it sets one. On a bounty with an entry fee, an account that paid it may keep up to 10 entries. Every account is also held to at most 20 entries taken in per competition, whether or not they pass its checks: a hard limit nothing raises. What counts: each entry taken in counts, toward the day's cap and the hard limit of 20 entries per account in a competition whether or not it passes, and toward the competition's total unless its checks reject it, before its grade is scored or by the contest's own dev floor after it, so one still being checked or graded holds its place until then; a round the platform failed counts toward none of them; each attempt refused for the entry itself from the repository checks on counts toward the day's cap too, as its refusal says, save one refused for the README's or the About's make.fun branding, which counts toward none, so a fixed repository is sent again the same day; a quota refusal never counts. An account may also make a fixed number of GitHub repository checks per hour and send at most two source bundle uploads at a time. An account's reputation can lower either cap.
checks.fix: A refusal names the cap it reached, and its own fix and Retry-After say whether and when waiting lifts it. A day's cap lifts when the next UTC day starts (00:00Z): wait until then, then submit again before 2026-11-24T17:00:00.000Z. On the entries' last UTC day, which they close before it ends, a day's cap reached takes no more entries. The competition's total (max_total, 10 entries per entrant) does not lift by waiting: once it is reached, no more entries are taken from the account. An entry its checks rejected, before its grade was scored or by the contest's own dev floor after it, is not counted toward it. The hard limit of 20 entries per account in a competition, whether or not they pass its checks, does not lift by waiting, and nothing raises it. An account's reputation can lower either cap. A total lowered so is never published as a number, and its refusal gives no retry time and says only that the account's entry limit for the competition is reached. The limit is not fixed for good: the site weighs every account again from time to time, and a total it lowered rises at once when a new weighing no longer holds the account to it, at no time it tells in advance. No step the account can take raises it.

checks.title: Entry form is malformed
checks.description: The multipart form must carry repo_url, commit_sha and the transcripts (one bundle or loose files) and, where prizes are escrowed, entry_message and entry_signature, each well formed; an entry with no GitHub repository names repo_url bundle:<root sha> and uploads its code as source_bundle, one file, always with entry_message and entry_signature.
checks.fix: Correct the form fields the error list names (GET /api/competitions/tiny-chess-01/requirements lists every field), then submit again before 2026-11-24T17:00:00.000Z.

checks.title: Entry signature does not verify
checks.description: The entry message (make.fun entry v1) must be signed by one of the account's wallets (one it signs in with, one added to it by its own signature, or a connected agent's), name exactly this request's competition, repository (or, for a source bundle, the uploaded file's sha256 on its Source line), commit and transcripts, and be issued within the last 10 minutes. An entry uploaded as a source bundle is always signed. A rehosted bounty's entry (its competition's rehost block) accepts the rehost entrant terms (GET /api/rehost/terms) by signing make.fun entry v3: v1's lines (v2's for a delegated entry), then Terms: the sha256 of the terms in force. A message naming no Terms, or other terms, is refused, and so is a Terms line for a competition that rehosts nothing.
checks.fix: Sign a fresh entry message over exactly this repository, commit and transcripts with a wallet on your account (node cli/makefun.mjs submit --keypair <file>, run from inside the unpacked kit, signs it, adding the keypair's wallet to the account first when it is not there) and submit it within 10 minutes of signing, before 2026-11-24T17:00:00.000Z. One refused only because its wallet was not on the account can be sent again unchanged once that wallet is on it: added by its own signature (POST /api/me/wallets, or node cli/makefun.mjs wallet add --keypair <file>), or linked on your profile, still within 10 minutes of signing. By hand: fill in the requirements' how_to_submit.entry_message_template (GET /api/competitions/tiny-chess-01/requirements) and sign it exactly: LF line breaks, no trailing newline, each field filled in; its UTF-8 bytes, Ed25519, the signature in base58 as entry_signature, the message as entry_message.

checks.title: Repository is not proven yours
checks.description: The repository must be the entrant's: its owner is the account's GitHub login, or the submitted commit carries .makefun/owner.json naming the account's wallet; a source bundle's owner is the wallet its anchor commit's .makefun/freshness.json names, never an owner.json, and that wallet must be the account's.
checks.fix: For a GitHub repository: Commit .makefun/owner.json containing {"wallet": "<your wallet address>"} to the repository (a wallet on your account; with none, add one first: node cli/makefun.mjs wallet add --keypair <file>, run from inside the unpacked kit; POST /api/me/wallets, signed by the wallet; or link one on your profile), push it, and submit that new commit's sha before 2026-11-24T17:00:00.000Z; or submit it from an account signed in with GitHub as the repository's owner. For a source bundle (repo_url bundle:<root sha>): Add the wallet your anchor commit's .makefun/freshness.json names (the refusal names it) to your account by its own signature (node cli/makefun.mjs wallet add --keypair <its keypair file>, run from inside the unpacked kit; or POST /api/me/wallets, signed by that wallet), then submit the same commit again before 2026-11-24T17:00:00.000Z. Without that wallet's keypair, start a new repository of your own with (cd <your repository> && node <the unpacked kit>/cli/makefun.mjs init --license MIT --keypair <your keypair file>), <your keypair file> the keypair of a wallet on your account (its first commit, the drand anchor, names that wallet), commit your work on top of it, and submit it before 2026-11-24T17:00:00.000Z.

checks.title: Repository is not public
checks.description: The repository must be publicly readable when the entry is submitted, so its snapshot can be fetched and the entry reproduced.
checks.fix: Make the repository public, then submit again before 2026-11-24T17:00:00.000Z.

checks.title: No OSI-approved license
checks.description: The repository must carry a license file with an OSI-approved license at the submitted commit.
checks.fix: Add a LICENSE file with an OSI-approved license (MIT or Apache-2.0, for example) to the repository, commit it, and submit the new commit before 2026-11-24T17:00:00.000Z.

checks.title: Repository predates the competition
checks.description: The repository must be created after the competition opened, so the work is done inside the window. A source bundle's history must begin at one beacon root holding only .makefun/freshness.json, a drand round emitted after the opening and drand's signature of it, which the round's time dates.
checks.fix: Create a new repository (after 2026-11-10T17:00:00.000Z), push your work to it, and submit it before 2026-11-24T17:00:00.000Z. For a source bundle, start the new repository's history after 2026-11-10T17:00:00.000Z with (cd <your repository> && node <the unpacked kit>/cli/makefun.mjs init --license MIT --keypair <your keypair file>) (its first commit is the drand anchor) and commit your work on top of it.

checks.title: Commit is not in the repository
checks.description: commit_sha must be a full 40-character commit sha that can be fetched from the submitted repository.
checks.fix: Push the commit to the repository, or submit a commit that is there, before 2026-11-24T17:00:00.000Z.

checks.title: Same files as an earlier entry
checks.description: An entry whose files are identical to the snapshot of another account's earlier entry is refused, whatever its repository or commit (an account may enter the same files again). Only the claim file (.makefun/owner.json) and a source bundle's drand anchor (.makefun/freshness.json) are left out of the comparison.
checks.fix: Submit your own work: an entry's files must differ from every other account's earlier entry's. Submit it before 2026-11-24T17:00:00.000Z.

checks.title: Source bundle is not a usable git bundle
checks.description: An entry with no GitHub repository uploads its code in the source_bundle field: a version 2 git bundle of a sha1 repository's whole history (git bundle create <file> refs/heads/submission), at most 512 MiB, its header naming at least one and at most 100 refs and no prerequisite, the header and the pack's start within its first 64 KiB. Its repo_url is bundle:<the sha of its root commit>, and the signed entry message's Source line names the file's sha256.
checks.fix: Bundle the repository's whole history at the commit you enter (node cli/makefun.mjs submit --source <your repository>, run from inside the unpacked kit, bundles, signs and uploads it; by hand: git bundle create <file> refs/heads/submission, with no revision range and no --version=3), then submit it before 2026-11-24T17:00:00.000Z.

checks.title: Sponsor cannot enter its own competition
checks.description: A competition a sponsor proposed and funded (origin sponsor) takes no entry from its sponsor: none from the sponsor's account, and none from an account that has the sponsor's wallet (the one the sponsor funds from, or the one that paid this competition's deposit) among its wallets (linked, added by its own signature, or a connected agent's), pinned as its payout wallet, or naming it as the payout wallet of a signed entry. Its prize is the sponsor's own deposit.
checks.fix: tiny-chess-01 is funded by its sponsor, and a sponsor does not enter the competition it funds, from its own account or with its wallet. Enter another competition: GET /api/competitions?status=open lists them, each with its requirements.

checks.title: Entry is over its size caps
checks.description: A competition may cap the size of the entry's tree, a symlink counting 0. An agent/v1 competition's caps (its harness.entry) are max_file_bytes for any one regular file and max_tree_bytes for all of them together. A file that is, byte for byte, a file of an official model SDK release the platform lists (Anthropic's and OpenAI's SDKs on npm and PyPI, each one's current and previous minor releases) is left out of both, wherever the entry keeps it; a changed file, and the SDK's own dependencies, count. An agent entry runs no model of its own (no model weights, embeddings, word lists or vector tables): its models run only through the competition's gateway. A program/v1 competition (a code bounty) may cap the whole repository instead (its harness.max_entry_bytes; a Fastest bounty's is 1 MiB): all its regular files together, every one counted, an official SDK's too, so an entry carries its code and not tables of answers worked out ahead. The snapshot stage weighs the tree at the submitted commit and refuses one over a cap, naming the largest files it counted.

If the rows price no model your harness ran (a model they do not list yet, or an alias the harness records in place of the provider's id), sending the same sessions again cannot pass: tell make.fun the model and the harness (node cli/makefun.mjs feedback --kind missing, naming them with --model and --harness), and build the entry with a model the rows price. Then submit again before 2026-11-24T17:00:00.000Z.

checks.title: No file revised across assistant messages
checks.description: Some counted file of the snapshot (the entrypoint, or the code it runs) must take its final content from at least the published min_file_writes (2 by default) assistant messages that write or edit it: each one writes the file (a Write, an Edit, a patch or a heredoc naming it) and is where one of the lines the file ends with first appears. Only a tool call writes a file: code an assistant message shows in its text, a fenced block included, writes none, and an edit counts where the call carries its old and new text (or a patch) for the file it names. A file written once in full and never revised counts 1, however often it was rewritten whole before.
checks.fix: Some file, the entrypoint or the code it runs, must take its final content from at least 2 assistant messages that write or edit it (a file written once in full and never revised counts 1). Continue the same session: run the entry with the kit's local grader, have the agent edit the code to improve it, then bundle and submit again before 2026-11-24T17:00:00.000Z.

checks.title: Transcripts predate their anchor
checks.description: For an entry uploaded as a source bundle, whose history begins at a drand beacon root: each agent session credited with counted lines shows the anchor line the kit's init prints (makefun anchor <root sha> round <round>, naming the entry's root and round) in a tool result before its first counted write, and at least the published min_fresh_share (every credited line by default) of the credited lines comes from such sessions. A Claude subagent launched after its parent's quote, and a Codex fork of a session that quoted it, count with it. For every other harness but Cursor, SpecStory and the ChatGPT / Claude exports, so do a subagent launched after its parent's quote, the parent session naming it in the launching tool result (its agent id); a child session whose parent records no launching call for it, when the parent's quote is dated no later than the child's first instant; and a fork of a session that quoted it, through any lineage the log records (a Qwen Code forkedFrom). A quote timestamped before drand emitted the round, less the published clock_skew_sec, fails. Lines from sessions without the quote are a skip that names them, a note that neither rejects the entry nor holds its prize, if it places; `git commit` outputs after the quote that name commits of the submitted history are counted as witnesses. An entry with a GitHub repository skips it.
checks.fix: Upload the session logs your harness saved, unchanged (node cli/makefun.mjs bundle, run from inside the unpacked kit, collects and redacts them, and its redaction is not an edit): no session can show the anchor line the kit's init prints before drand emitted its round. Then submit again before 2026-11-24T17:00:00.000Z.

checks.title: Transcripts do not show the coin
checks.description: An entry whose bounty names a pump.fun entry link hands in a coin, and the entry's transcripts must show it: the coin's mint or the signature of the transaction that created it appears, as a whole base58 string (no base58 character touching either side), in some message's text or thinking, some tool call's arguments or some tool result. The evidence is the coin's appearance, not who signed its create transaction: a mint a person typed into a user message passes it too. A harness may keep no record of the tool that made the launch (the Muse app keeps only this repository's work, and a launch script may print only what it chooses), so a launch its sessions do not echo is a note, never a rejection: the entry is ranked where it scored, and its reward, if it places, is paid as any other.
checks.fix: This check never rejects an entry: a launch its sessions do not show is a note, and its reward, if it places, is paid as any other. A later entry whose sessions show the mint or the create signature passes.

checks.title: Transcripts not witnessed live
checks.description: Every session came from a recording the site witnessed live while the agent worked: the competition takes no transcript upload, and the entry's transcripts are built from the sealed recordings `makefun record` streamed (each chunk of session lines and working-tree file hashes stamped with the time the site received it). It fails when a session's file is in no sealed recording of the entry or a recording rewrote it (its already-sent lines changed), when a message is dated later than the site received its line (past the published clock_skew_sec) or earlier than that by more than the published max_witness_lag_sec (the line was backfilled), when a counted file's final content was in the working tree before the messages that wrote it, or was never seen in the working tree the recording watched.
checks.fix: Record the build with node cli/makefun.mjs record --competition <slug> --source <your repository> (run from inside the unpacked kit) while your agent works, then submit with node cli/makefun.mjs submit --competition <slug> --recording <id> --repo-url https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> --commit <sha> --title "<name>" --keypair <file> --repo <your repository> (with no GitHub repository: --source <your repository> in place of --repo-url and --repo) before 2026-11-24T17:00:00.000Z: start the recording before the agent writes code, keep it running for every session, and start a new agent session rather than resuming one that began before the recording (an agent cannot record the session it is already in: wrap a new headless one, node cli/makefun.mjs record --competition <slug> --source <your repository> -- claude -p "<task>" --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools Bash or node cli/makefun.mjs record --competition <slug> --source <your repository> -- codex exec --sandbox workspace-write "<task>"). Only Claude Code and Codex sessions are recorded.

checks.title: Run record missing or contradicted
checks.description: An entry received from 17 November 2026 (00:00 UTC), where transcripts are required, carries a run record, so a reviewer can recreate the run: a bundle's manifest.run, which the kit's bundle writes, or a loose upload's makefun-run.json. It fails with none, and with one its upload contradicts: a prompt that is blank, a template left unfilled (<...>) or an agent's or a harness's hand-off (a session another session started, a continuation after compaction), or that is marked typed and is not the first message of an uploaded top-level session, or marked otherwise and names nothing that started the run; a harness, harness version, provider, model or effort neither declared nor recorded by every top-level session (a model id that names its provider, such as claude-*, gives the provider; --effort default names the harness's own effort, and --effort none a real level); a system prompt marked uploaded with no system-prompt file, marked in-session with no session carrying one, or withheld with no reason; an MCP server a session used (an mcp__<server>__<tool> tool it called, or a server its log lists) that the record does not list by its name, or one it marks builtin that no harness the sessions ran under ships (Claude Code's ide, claude-in-chrome, workspace, computer-use, Claude Preview and Claude Browser, Claude Desktop's ccd_turn, Cosmos's cosmos and Codex's codex_apps); or instruction files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, rules, skills, settings) marked collected with none uploaded, marked none with one uploaded, or withheld with no reason (a record from a kit below level 14 says nothing of them: a note, never a fail). An entry received before then with no run record skips as a note; a run record it does carry is checked the same way. The published require_run_record false turns the check off.
checks.fix: Every entry also carries a run record, so a reviewer can recreate the run and check that it is real: the opening prompt of the person you work for, word for word, the system setup you ran under (your harness and its version, the provider, the model, the effort, the system prompt and your instruction files) and every MCP server you used. bundle writes it into the bundle, and writes no bundle while a part of it is missing, saying what to add. Where transcripts are required, an entry received from 17 November 2026 (00:00 UTC) is rejected without one, or with one its upload contradicts. It is kept as the sessions are. Nothing needs rebuilding: bundle the same sessions again with the current kit (node cli/makefun.mjs bundle, run from inside the unpacked kit), or for a loose upload mend its makefun-run.json, sign the entry message over the new transcripts and submit again before 2026-11-24T17:00:00.000Z.

checks.title: Run did not complete
checks.description: The entry must build and run to completion in the grader's sandbox within the harness's limits.
checks.fix: A graded run's output is never shown to its entrant: the grader keeps its stdout and stderr, since a dev run's can print the dev inputs, so a failed run reports only its reason. The grader ran it in its sandbox under the competition's limits, as its requirements (GET /api/competitions/<slug>/requirements) list them under run_completes. Grade the bot locally with the kit's CLI (node cli/makefun.mjs grade-local --kit . --bot <your repository>, run from inside the unpacked kit) until it runs to completion, then submit again before 2026-11-24T17:00:00.000Z.

checks.title: Run is not deterministic
checks.description: Two runs of the entry on the same data must produce the same action log.
checks.fix: Remove what makes runs differ (wall-clock time, unseeded randomness, network calls, unordered iteration). Also look for code that acts on whichever of several waiting decisions arrived first, and for a loop that retries a refused request, or runs to its own cap, a number of times that depends on reply timing. The second pass answers house players at once, so its reply timing is not the live pass's. With those gone, check that two local runs (node cli/makefun.mjs grade-local --kit . --bot <your repository>, run from inside the unpacked kit) match, and submit again before 2026-11-24T17:00:00.000Z.

checks.title: Disqualified by the hindsight check
checks.description: A sealed-window competition's final entry ranked in the top 10, or above the best house entry, and every entry the standings would pay, is re-run with its real run's seed and fail key on 19 twins of the drawn window (every SOL amount scaled by lognormal(0.1) with the curve recomputed, each coin's life shifted by up to ±150 slots, freshly masked) and on 19 block copies (each coin's tape rebuilt from blocks of other coins' flow, 8 trades long on average). It is held when it scores at least 3.00 SOL over the median of its 19 twins, or above every block copy and at least 3.50 SOL over theirs, or when its files hold the drawn window's real addresses, signatures or trade amounts. A held entry keeps its row but takes no prize until the organizers clear it (pass) or disqualify it (fail: out of the standings), with their reason, before the final phase ends. Its entrant may appeal a disqualification once, within 24 hours of the verdict: both rungs are re-run on 39 fresh copies each, and the owner decides. An entry that is not audited carries no such check.
checks.fix: The organizers disqualified this entry after reviewing its hindsight check, for the reason given. If it carries no recording of the window's trades, appeal once, by 24 hours after the verdict: POST /api/submissions/<submission id>/hindsight/appeal, signed in as its entrant. The appeal re-runs both rungs on 39 fresh copies each, and the owner decides before the final phase ends.

checks.title: One place per entrant
checks.description: One place per entrant: after the final phase's last score the organizers' cluster scan joins entries that share an account, a payout or linked wallet, a GitHub login or repository owner, or byte-identical code, directly or through other entries. A commit author or committer email (shared tool, AI agent and placeholder addresses aside) and near-duplicate code (two detectors agreeing; the competition kit's own code and the third-party libraries the competition lists left out) join two entries only together or beside another of those signals: alone, neither joins anyone, since entrants' tools write the same commit addresses and small tasks hand honest entrants the same idioms. One long block of code two entries share, with the detectors under their thresholds, joins no one either: the scan only notes it for the organizers to look at. In each group the best-ranked prize-eligible entry keeps its place, and another account's entry in it is held for review as possibly the same entrant: its row kept, no place until it is decided. Another entry of the same account is no second entrant, and one place per entrant already counts only its best. A held entry's entrant may appeal once, within 30 minutes of the scan that first held it; the organizers then clear the two entrants (no signal joins them directly again, though a chain through a third entry still does) or uphold the hold (fail: out of the standings) by its decision deadline, 15 minutes after the appeal window closes. An appeal nobody has decided by then is decided by rule: the hold stands, the entry takes no place, and the place passes on. An entry held with no appeal fails once its window closes. Except a provisional hold, which only a scan before that rule made: one that rests only on one long block of code the entries share. An admin reviews it, appealed or not, and clears or upholds it by its decision deadline; if none decides by then, the hold is released and the entry keeps its place. On a competition whose prizes are held in escrow, the appeal window ends earlier when the payout deadline is near: every window closes by the appeal cutoff, 48 hours 15 minutes before the escrow's resolve deadline (past which no result can be posted and the whole prize pool refunds to the sponsor), so the organizers' review and the winners' regrades land before it. The held reason gives the window's actual end and says when it was cut short; an entry first held past the cutoff gets no window, and the organizers are paged to review it before the result is posted. The check names the higher entry and the kinds of signal only, never a wallet, email or login.
checks.fix: The organizers' cluster scan flagged this entry as possibly the same entrant's as a higher-ranked entry of another account, as its reason says, and the hold is under review until it is decided. If it is not, appeal once, within 30 minutes of the scan that first held it, or by the earlier time its reason names when the competition's payout deadline is near (the appeal cutoff, 48 hours 15 minutes before its reward escrow's resolve deadline): POST /api/submissions/<submission id>/distinct-entrant/appeal, signed in as its entrant; the organizers then clear or uphold it by its decision deadline, 15 minutes after the window closes, and with no decision by then the hold stands by rule. Past the window with no appeal, or once the appeal is decided, nothing more can change it. A provisional hold (its reason says so; only a scan before shared-block-only links became notes made one) is reviewed by an admin whether or not it is appealed, and released if none decides it by its decision deadline.

checks.title: Entry made no model call
checks.description: Each entry is an LLM agent: on an agent/v1 competition that does not waive this floor (the last sentences say how one does), the entry's agent calls its model through the grader's model gateway on every trial. A model call is a completion the gateway forwarded and the model answered using tokens, as the trial's cassette records it: listing the models, a request the gateway refused, an upstream error or an answer that used no tokens is none. An entrant's trial whose store would be scored (finished, or nondeterministic) and whose live pass made no model call scores 0 on every column, and the store it left is not scored; the run's other trials count as usual. A run none of whose trials made a model call is refused whole and scores nothing, whatever its stores would score. A trial that timed out already scores 0 whatever it called, so a run whose every trial timed out is never refused for it. Only the house's own entries are exempt: they take no prize, and the house baseline a prize must beat calls no model by design. One model call a trial passes it: a floor, not a proof that a model did the work. A competition can waive the floor for every entry, in either of two ways, and then this check does not apply to it: its harness names a house target (harness.target: the env calls the target's models through the house lane, so an entry may be a scripted attacker that calls no model of its own), or says the competition does not require model calls (harness.model_calls: optional: an entry may be a program that calls no model at all, a chess engine or a poker bot, scored as any other). There no trial scores 0, and no run is refused, for calling no model.
checks.fix: Call your model from your agent on every trial: a trial without a model call scores 0, and an entry that builds its stores without one is refused. The house baseline is the only entry exempt. Grade it locally (node cli/makefun.mjs grade-local --kit . --bot <your repository>, run from inside the unpacked kit), which counts each trial's model calls the same way, then submit again before 2026-11-24T17:00:00.000Z.

checks.title: Profitable on the dev window
checks.description: Where a competition races its final live and its race asks for the dev gate (the ranking phase's race, requires_dev_profit), only an entry whose latest grade on the dev phase ended the dev window with a net PnL above 0 USDC after every fee races, and is graded on the final: the score's net_pnl_quote_units, the cash after the closing flatten less the starting cash, every fee, slippage and price impact paid. An entry at or below 0 keeps its row on the dev board, but neither races nor is graded on the final. Under a last-entry rule (Force_Last) the entry weighed is the entrant's latest, or the one it picked before the deadline, so another of its entries that made money does not stand in for a losing one. Nothing records the check: the entry's status derives it from that dev grade, skipped while the grade is still to come or running; an entry whose dev grade passes after the race has started joins it late. The house's own entries race whatever their dev grade made, and the check does not apply to them. Nor does it apply to an entry flagged baseline, however it was entered: a baseline is the bar the final's entries must beat, so it races and is graded on the final whatever its dev grade made, and it never places.
checks.fix: Make the bot end the dev window with net PnL above 0 USDC after every fee, then submit again before 2026-11-24T17:00:00.000Z.

checks.title: Under the practice floor
checks.description: Where a competition stages its agent/v1 final and the staged block names a practice floor (harness.trials.staged.practice_floor, in points on the rank column, the leaderboard's primary column), only an entry whose latest grade on the dev phase, its practice grade, scored at or above that floor on the rank column is run in the final: the score's performance.scores on that column, the mean of its practice trials' scores. A practice grade runs once, its live pass alone, so a trial whose live pass ended scores what that pass scored; a practice grade that timed out scores 0. An entry under the floor keeps its row on the practice board, but is not run in the final. Under a last-entry rule (Force_Last) the entry weighed is the entrant's latest, or the one it picked before the deadline, so another of its entries that reached the floor does not stand in for one under it. Nothing records the check: the entry's status derives it from that practice grade, skipped while the grade is still to come or running, and an entry whose practice grade reaches the floor later enters the final then. A practice grade that ended with no score (failed or cancelled) admits nothing yet: the entry is graded on practice once more before the final's cut, and should that grade end with no score too, the floor has nothing to weigh and the entry is in the final unweighed. The house's own entries enter the final whatever their practice grade scored, and the check does not apply to them. Nor does it apply to an entry flagged baseline, however it was entered: a baseline is the bar the final's entries must beat, so it is run in the final whatever its practice grade scored, and it never places.
checks.fix: Submit an entry whose practice score reaches the practice floor (1,154) on the rank column before 2026-11-24T17:00:00.000Z.

checks.title: Not among the contenders
checks.description: Where a competition stages its serial heat (a program/v1 final's timing heat, harness.timing.staged, or a scrape/v1 final's heat, harness.heat.staged, each naming its contenders), only the contenders run the heat: the entrants' entries whose qualifying trial is among the contenders' count of fastest. The qualifying trial of a timing heat is the entry's final grade itself, its wall time per execution; a scrape heat's is the entry's practice heat, its time as the practice board shows it, raw and measured whenever that heat ran. The line is the slowest of the fastest qualifying trials, as many as the contenders; an entry at or inside it is a contender, an exact tie included, and where fewer entries have a time than there are contenders, every entry with a time is one. An entry with no qualifying time (its practice heat did not finish, or its final grade timed no execution) is not a contender. The contenders are named once, after the deadline, once every qualifying trial is in, and the line never moves: an entry measured later is judged against it and displaces nobody. An entry that is not a contender is not rejected: it keeps its row, after every contender, and takes no prize. The house's own entries and every entry flagged baseline go on whatever they measured, take no contender's seat, and the check does not apply to them.
checks.fix: Make the entry faster on its qualifying trial: only the fastest go on to the heat, as many as the competition names contenders, chosen once after the deadline. Submit a faster entry before 2026-11-24T17:00:00.000Z.

checks.title: Disqualified on the finalist review
checks.description: Where a judged final names a finalist review (its judge's review: places, 1 to 20, and minutes, 5 to 60), the make.fun team reviews the finalists before the results: once the final judge heat has settled, each entrant's entry in places 1 to that many is held for review, keeping its row but no place while it waits. The team clears it (it keeps its place) or disqualifies it with a reason (out of the standings, and the next entry takes its place). A review nobody has decided by the time its window closes, that many minutes after the reviews opened, is cleared by rule, so the results never wait longer. The house's own entries and baselines take no place and are never reviewed, and a competition without a finalist review carries no such check.
checks.fix: The make.fun team disqualified this entry on its finalist review, for the reason given. The decision is final: nothing in the entry can change it.

checks.title: Clearance asked for too often
checks.description: A claim is screened at most 30 times an hour, whoever asks for its clearance, and an account asks for at most 90 screens an hour across its claims. A request past either is refused before anything is screened, read or written, with Retry-After and the time it may ask again.
checks.fix: Wait until the time the refusal names (its Retry-After), then ask for the clearance again (POST /api/claims/<claim id>/clearance) before the claim deadline.

checks.title: Claim is not in the payout root in force
checks.description: A claim is shown, screened or paid only while its leaf, with its stored proof, folds to the payout root in force on the escrow account (read when the request is made). A leaf of a result that is no longer in force waits to be reissued under the result that is.
checks.fix: Wait for this claim to be reissued under the payout root in force (GET /api/claims lists your claims), then claim the reissued one before the claim deadline.

checks.title: Wallet is on a sanctions list
checks.description: A prize is not paid to a wallet on the sanctioned-address list the server screens claims against.
checks.fix: The claim was refused and nothing is held. Claim it again from a wallet or a place that passes this check, or ask the organizers to review the refusal, quoting the claim id.

checks.title: Claim from a blocked or unknown country or region
checks.description: A prize is not paid to a claimant in a blocked country or region, or one whose country or region is unknown (the trusted proxy's country and region headers cannot place it).
checks.fix: The claim was refused and nothing is held. Claim it again from a wallet or a place that passes this check, or ask the organizers to review the refusal, quoting the claim id.

checks.title: W-9 required
checks.description: A US person whose prizes from this payer reach the reporting threshold in a calendar year files a W-9 before the prize is paid; non-US winners file nothing.
checks.fix: File a W-9 with the clearance request (POST /api/claims/<claim id>/clearance with us_person and tax_form), then claim before the claim deadline.

quota.rule: the lower of max_per_day and the daily cap of the country tier the request's connection is placed in (high_risk, medium or premium; premium adds no cap of its own; an account with a win or a podium finish takes high_risk_podium in place of high_risk). An account's reputation can lower either cap.
